newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes mostly firm, oil slick supportive.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes mostly firm, oil slick supportive.

text.p: Cash crude prices in Asia were mostly firmer on Monday and premiums steady in generally hesitant trading as sentiment for medium grades were mildly underpinned by the oil slick offshore Japan, market sources said.

Traders said the threat of an oil slick affecting nuclear power stations in Japan was helping sentiment of medium grades that might be in demand should nuclear power stations reduce output or shut down.
Two layers of sea fences were being put up around inlet pipes for the nuclear plants to keep the oil slick from the stricken Nakhodka from affecting the plants.
Traders said there had been no price reaction to the oil slick, but it was mildly underpinning sentiment for other potential power fuels like medium graded crudes.
Traders said they heard two February Minas deals done into China from Japanese traders, one at ICP plus $1.09 and the other at ICP plus $1.15.
January Minas went out at ICP plus almost 90 cents and traders said the increased premium level for February was the result of demand from China.
Paper levels in Singapore were stable from Friday and little changed from New York.
Traders said they expected the Dubai market to be underpinned this week in expectation India would issues a monthly tender to buy March.
Tapis paper edged up five cents. February was quoted at $25.30/$25.50, indicating at outright physical price of more than $27.00 per barrel.
